title: Food Safety Officer
raw_text:
8-640. Military Occupational Specialty 640A--Food Safety Officer
   a. Licensing/certification requirement. None.
   b. Prerequisites. DA Cir 601 series.
   c. MOS 640A. MOS 640A is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOS are 68R or 68S
MOS, NCOES, grade and time-in-service prerequisites can be waived if the applicant has a BS or
MS degree in one of these specialties: Food Science, Food Technology, Food Chemistry, Food
Microbiology, Food Quality Assurance, Food Defense, Quality Engineering, Public Health,
Environmental Health or Environmental Sanitation. Requests for waivers must be routed through
the Food Safety Warrant Officer Consultant, subject to approval by the Chief, Veterinary Corps.
   d. Associated SQI.
        (1) 0--No special qualifications.
        (2) 8--Instructor.
        (3) P--Parachutist.
        (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
        (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
   e. Associated ASI.
        (1) 2B--Air Assault (personnel only).
        (2) 3R--Force Management.
        (3) 5W--Jumpmaster (personnel only).
        (4) 6M--Mobilization and Demobilization Operations.
        (5) 6P--Master Fitness Trainer.
        (6) 6T--Military Auditor (Reserve Component personnel only).
        (7) 7Q--Training Development.
        (8) Q6--Protection Cell Operations (personnel only) (Effective 202410).
   f. Qualifications.
        (1) WO1 must--
              (a) Complete Warrant Officer Candidate School.
              (b) Have an associate degree or higher from an accredited college.
              (c) Be a U.S. citizen. Qualify for a security clearance of SECRET.
        (2) CW2 must—
              (a) Meet the qualifications described in paragraph f(1).
              (b) Complete the Veterinary Corps Food Safety Officer Basic Course (640A).
        (3) CW3 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(2).
              (b) Complete the AMEDD Captain’s Career Course (that includes the Food Safety
Warrant Officer Advanced Technical Track).
              (c) Complete the Action Officer Development Course (ACCP 13 POO) by distance
learning.
              (d) Obtain a BS/MS food science degree or related discipline for assignment to
designated key positions.
        (4) CW4 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(3).
              (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Staff Course (WOSC), including the Food Safety
Officer WOSC follow-on course.
              (c) Obtain a BS/MS food science degree or related discipline for assignment to
designated key positions.
        (5) CW5 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(4).
              (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Senior Staff Course (WOSSC).
              (c) Obtain a BS/MS food science degree or related discipline for assignment to
designated key positions.
   g. Duties.
        (1) WO1/CW2--
              (a) Manages and directs military food safety and quality assurance programs to
include personnel, facilities, and equipment under the guidance and supervision of the senior
Veterinary Corps Officer (VCO).
               (b) Organizes and conducts commercial sanitation audits and military sanitation
inspections, recognizes sanitation deficiencies, and determines sanitary compliance ratings of
civilian and government facilities that produce, process, prepare, manufacture, store, or otherwise
handle subsistence.
              (c) Provides technical advice concerning food safety, food defense, quality assurance
issues to Medical Brigade/Group Command and Staff, military acquisition, supply, and retail
activities.
              (d) Identifies and provides technical information concerning microbiological, chemical,
and physical deterioration of subsistence.
              (e) Interfaces with DoD, Federal, State, local, and host-nation inspection authorities
and regulatory health agencies concerning food safety and quality assurance matters.
              (f) Observes, records, and reports on subsistence problems that may have public
health significance.
              (g) Interviews patients and collects data on food borne disease of public health
significance to assist epidemiological investigations.
              (h) Develops/conducts food safety and quality assurance training to support local unit
mission requirements.
         (2) CW3--
              (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(1).
              (b) Provides supervision/guidance for food safety, food defense and quality
assurance programs in a tactical environment at Division/Corps level to include slaughter and
processing of food animals in emergency situations and the procurement of food stocks from
foreign establishments.
              (c) Provides technical advice on food safety, food defense, and quality assurance
engineering principles for the acquisition, assembly, storage, and distribution of operational
rations for DoD.
         (3) CW4--
              (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(2).
              (b) Provides guidance for food safety, food defense and quality assurance programs
to subordinate food inspection elements or other staff elements in a tactical environment at
echelons above Corps or at a Major Medical Command Regional Medical Center.
              (c) Serves as the technical consultant on the staff of the Senior Veterinary Officer
within a tactical theater of operations or at a Major Medical Command Regional Medical Center
concerning all food inspection matters.
              (d) Provides guidance and technical advice concerning Statistical Process Control
(SPC), Systems Auditing, Total Quality Management (TQM), and other quality engineering
programs as a Quality Engineer at selected positions on the senior staff at a Major Medical
Command or DoD Acquisition Agency Headquarters.
         (4) CW5--
              (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(3).
              (b) Serves as the technical consultant on the staff of the Senior Veterinary Officer at
a Major Medical Command concerning all food inspection matters.
              (c) Provides guidance and technical advice to subordinate food inspection elements
or other staff elements providing food inspection support to all levels of the Armed Forces.
              (d) May serve as the Chief Warrant Officer of the Veterinary Corps Branch and
Consultant to the Chief of the Veterinary Corps and the Surgeon General.
    h. Physical Demands Rating and qualifications for initial awarding of MOS.
      (1) Have 20/20 correctable vision, normal color discrimination per AR 40-501, full use of both
hands, and a keen sense of smell.
      (2) A physical profile of 222222.
      (3) A Physical demands rating of Moderate (Gold).
      (4) Qualifying Scores: A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) – 0120 cm.,
Seated Power Throw (PT) – 0350 cm., Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0120 cm., and Interval Aerobic
Run (IR) – 0036 shuttles in Physical Demand Category “Moderate” (Gold).
      (5) Table 8-640A-1. Physical requirements.
       (6) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels: W2
equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are
listed in the following standards of grade tables:
           (a) Table 8-640A-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
           (b) Table 8-640A-3. Standards of grade TDA.

(a) Manages and directs military food safety and quality assurance programs to include personnel, facilities, and equipment under the guidance and supervision of the senior Veterinary Corps Officer (VCO).
Monitor sanitation practices to ensure that employees follow standards and regulations.

(b) Organizes and conducts commercial sanitation audits and military sanitation inspections, recognizes sanitation deficiencies, and determines sanitary compliance ratings of civilian and government facilities that produce, process, prepare, manufacture, store, or otherwise handle subsistence.

Advise food service managers and organizations on sanitation, safety procedures, menu development, budgeting, and planning to assist with establishment, operation, and evaluation of food service facilities and nutrition programs.
(c) Provides technical advice concerning food safety, food defense, quality assurance issues to Medical Brigade/Group Command and Staff, military acquisition, supply, and retail activities.
Examine physiological, morphological, and cultural characteristics, using microscope, to identify and classify microorganisms in human, water, and food specimens.
(d) Identifies and provides technical information concerning microbiological, chemical, and physical deterioration of subsistence.
Inspect food processing areas to ensure compliance with government regulations and standards for sanitation, safety, quality, and waste management.
(e) Interfaces with DoD, Federal, State, local, and host-nation inspection authorities and regulatory health agencies concerning food safety and quality assurance matters.
Report patterns of patients' health conditions, such as disease status and births, to public health agencies.
(f) Observes, records, and reports on subsistence problems that may have public health significance.
Perform epidemiological investigations of acute and chronic diseases.
(g) Interviews patients and collects data on food borne disease of public health significance to assist epidemiological investigations.
Evaluate food processing and storage operations and assist in the development of quality assurance programs for such operations.
(h) Develops/conducts food safety and quality assurance training to support local unit mission requirements.
Assign and review the work of subordinates.

Monitor the operations and sanitary conditions of slaughtering or meat processing plants.

(c) Provides technical advice on food safety, food defense, and quality assurance engineering principles for the acquisition, assembly, storage, and distribution of operational rations for DoD.

(b) Provides guidance for food safety, food defense and quality assurance programs to subordinate food inspection elements or other staff elements in a tactical environment at echelons above Corps or at a Major Medical Command Regional Medical Center.
Provide consultative services in areas such as equipment or product evaluation, plant construction or layout, or food safety systems.

(c) Serves as the technical consultant on the staff of the Senior Veterinary Officer within a tactical theater of operations or at a Major Medical Command Regional Medical Center concerning all food inspection matters.
Serve as a technical liaison between quality control and other departments, vendors, or contractors.

(d) Provides guidance and technical advice concerning Statistical Process Control (SPC), Systems Auditing, Total Quality Management (TQM), and other quality engineering programs as a Quality Engineer at selected positions on the senior staff at a Major Medical Command or DoD Acquisition Agency Headquarters.

(b) Serves as the technical consultant on the staff of the Senior Veterinary Officer at a Major Medical Command concerning all food inspection matters.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
